title: POC weekly - Latency Pulse checkpoint
topics: next steps for benchmark and pilot expansion
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on recent TTFT regression after a kernel path update. SE presented microbenchmarks showing variance at short sequences; customer outlined production traffic shape and concerns about cost vs latency. Agreed to run targeted microbench with quant profiles and a small canary on dedicated pool. Actions: Redwood to share trimmed benchmark script, customer to provide 5k sample requests and SLOs, schedule midweek handoff for private deployment checklist.

transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-04-14 16:00 UTC; Duration: ~62 minutes; Recording: yes
Attendees: Mark Hargreaves (Redwood AE), Priya Anand (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SRE), Jason Liu (BlueArc ML Eng), Asha Patel (BlueArc Platform), Tom Reynolds (BlueArc Infra), Sophie Grant (BlueArc PM)

[00:00] Mark (Redwood): Okay, everyone, thanks for joining. Quick note, we'll keep to the usual 60 min. Priya will run through the microbench results and then we'll get into the production traffic shape and next steps.
[00:22] Priya (Redwood): Cool. hi hi. So last night we pushed the kernel path change to the test harness — this was the one that selects the tiled matmul for short seqlen — and we saw a TTFT bump for sequences under 32 tokens. I have slides but I'll share the raw numbers first. P50 went from ~18ms to ~29ms on GTX-class nodes for the small prompt bucket, p95 spiked to about 110ms in microburst.
[00:47] Jason (BlueArc): Wait 110ms p95 for short ones? That can't happen for our chat replies, that's, that's above our SLO. Our product SLO is 80ms p95 for first token for interactive features.
[01:10] Priya (Redwood): Yeah and we dug in — it's not purely compute; the tiled matmul path increases kernel dispatch overhead for very short sequences and the streaming handshake amplifies microburst queuing. There's also a KV cache warmup effect in our harness.
[01:39] Tom (BlueArc): Is that something that only appears on GTX or also on A100s? We're running a mix in staging.
[01:52] Priya (Redwood): Good question. We ran across both. On A100 the delta is smaller — p50 from 12 -> 16ms, p95 60 -> 78ms — so it's still noticeable. We think kernel selection heuristics need a seqlen threshold bump.
[02:14] Sophie (BlueArc): Can you explain the streaming handshake bit? I thought streaming was just chunked response and not impacting first token.
[02:29] Luis (Redwood): The handshake is the initial sync of the stream and batching decisions; if a small request lands while a bigger batch is in flight the runtime can insert a short wait to avoid kernel thrash. That wait shows up as TTFT.
[02:49] Mark (Redwood): To add, our hedging/fallback routing can help — we can route short requests to a fast-path variant or a cached KV-primed instance. But that costs in terms of provisioned capacity.
[03:08] Asha (BlueArc): Cost is a concern. We don't want to overprovision for every short chat; our product team will push back if infra costs jump.
[03:22] Priya (Redwood): Totally. That's why the microbench showed options: keep current kernel with heuristics, or revert for sub-32 sequences and use the previous kernel there; or enable prefix caching for interactive sessions. Each has cost/complexity tradeoffs.
[03:45] Jason (BlueArc): What's the easiest/fastest mitigation? We're under time pressure to keep SLOs for the demo next month.
[03:56] Priya (Redwood): Short term: adjust kernel selection threshold to favor the older path for seqlen < 32. That is a config change we can canary in 24–48 hours. Medium term: prefix/KV warmup or a small dedicated fast-path pool.
[04:14] Mark (Redwood): We also recommended a trimmed benchmark you can run against your real payloads; if you provide a 5k sample set we can run repeatable trials and show delta charts.
[04:30] Jason (BlueArc): We'll do that. I can anonymize and upload tonight.
[04:38] Priya (Redwood): Great — note that in our runs we saw the p95 variance correlated with microburst arrival rates, so please include timestamps or inter-arrival info if possible.
[04:56] Sophie (BlueArc): Quick clarification — does KV caching require any app changes?
[05:06] Luis (Redwood): Minimal. You can pass a session id header to route to a warmed instance or enable client-side priming. We have docs, but for POC we can simulate.
[05:22] Tom (BlueArc): From infra side, network egress and VPC routing matter; if we go dedicated we need VPC peering and firewall rules. Is there a checklist?
[05:34] Mark (Redwood): Yes, we'll share the Private deploy checklist and a network diagram. Luis will help with port lists and certs.
[05:46] Luis (Redwood): I'll post a concise runbook.
[06:00] [00:06:00] Priya (Redwood): Ok slides page 2: here's the raw microbench output — note the bucketed seqlen histograms. For 8-16 tokens the per-request kernel dispatch overhead dominates. The tiled matmul is great for longer contexts but not micro replies.
[06:26] Jason (BlueArc): Our production seqlen median is 18, 90th is about 43. We bias toward shorter replies because of the UX.
[06:40] Priya (Redwood): That explains why the impact is material. I'm going to propose three experiments: 1) adjust kernel threshold for short seqlen; 2) temp small dedicated pool for hedged short requests; 3) run prefix-priming simulation.
[06:58] Asha (BlueArc): For experiment 2, how much would that cost? We need a ballpark.
[07:06] Luis (Redwood): Rough ballpark: a small dedicated pool (4 GPUs) for canary traffic for 48h would be ~$1200 in our estimate, cheaper if you already have reserved capacity. We'll send a precise estimate.
[07:20] Mark (Redwood): Also competitor note — I know CloudEndpointX offers ephemeral fast-path instances but it requires re-architecting client calls. We think our hedging approach is lower friction.
[07:36] Tom (BlueArc): We have a security checklist — SOC2, audit logs, KMS. Are there any blockers for a Private trial?
[07:48] Mark (Redwood): No known blockers. We have SOC2 docs and KMS integrations. Private requires some network setup and an access review. We'll share our compliance packet.
[08:02] Jason (BlueArc): One more thing — do you support SAML SSO for same portal?
[08:08] Mark (Redwood): Yes, we do SAML and can integrate with your IdP.
[08:13] [00:08:13] Priya (Redwood): I want to surface one oddity — in one run we saw a jittery p50 for long sequences when streaming is enabled; suspect interleaving of streaming chunk flushes and partial KV writes. Might be a subtle scheduling issue.
[08:32] Jason (BlueArc): That's worrying for longer generation tasks we run for reports.
[08:38] Priya (Redwood): We'll include those samples in the microbench run and add streaming vs non-streaming comparison.
[08:47] Sophie (BlueArc): Ok, timeline — we need a demo in three weeks. What can we guarantee by then?
[08:55] Mark (Redwood): By the demo we can canary the kernel threshold change and run a 48h canary comparing TTFT p50/p95. If that meets your SLO we can roll to more traffic. If not, we escalate to prefix-priming or the dedicated pool.
[09:12] Asha (BlueArc): Sounds reasonable. One more ask: can Redwood provide an estimated unit cost delta if we enable a dedicated fast-path? Our CFO will need a line item.
[09:24] Luis (Redwood): We'll provide a modeled delta: cost per 1k short requests with/without dedicated pool. I'll attach a spreadsheet.
[09:36] [00:09:36] Mark (Redwood): Ok moving to specific data we need from BlueArc — Jason, you said you'll upload 5k anonymized requests and the seqlen histogram, plus arrival timestamps if possible.
[09:50] Jason (BlueArc): Yep, I'll get that to the S3 link.
[09:56] Priya (Redwood): Also if you can share a couple of failing traces that show high TTFT that would speed debugging.
[10:03] Jason (BlueArc): I'll pick a few.
[10:08] [00:10:08] Priya (Redwood): Now, quick live demo of the trimmed harness — bear with me, I'll run two short runs back-to-back.
[10:18] [00:10:18] (background typing)
[10:27] Priya (Redwood): First run uses kernel A (legacy); p50 ~17ms p95 ~72ms for this sample. Second run with kernel B (tiled) shows p50 ~29ms p95 ~110ms for the short bucket, longer sequences improved marginally.
[10:45] Tom (BlueArc): That's very clear.
[10:48] Sophie (BlueArc): Can you attach the run artifacts after the call?
[10:53] Priya (Redwood): Yes, posting link in notes.
[10:57] [00:10:57] Mark (Redwood): Quick interjection — there may be perf regression due to a recent driver update on some host types; Luis, any insight?
[11:05] Luis (Redwood): We did a host kernel/driver bump on a subset of nodes last week. We're validating rollback but the regression pattern lines up more closely with kernel selection than driver changes. We'll still rule it out.
[11:20] Jason (BlueArc): Ok, for the canary, can we restrict to region eu-west-1? We want to test closest to our users.
[11:29] Mark (Redwood): Absolutely. We'll scope the pool to eu-west-1.
[11:34] [00:11:34] Priya (Redwood): One more data point — we observed that enabling batching window at 8ms reduces p95 for short sequences but increases p50 a touch. That's another knob.
[11:50] Asha (BlueArc): That tradeoff might be acceptable if it stabilizes p95. UX cares more about tail.
[11:57] Priya (Redwood): Understood. We'll include an experiment varying batching windows: 0ms, 4ms, 8ms.
[12:05] Mark (Redwood): Let's go through the timeline and owners briefly.
[12:10] [00:12:10] Action recap — Priya will share trimmed bench, Luis will send cost model and network runbook, Jason/Asha will provide samples and confirm stakeholders; we plan to run canary in eu-west-1 in ~48 hours.
[12:26] Sophie (BlueArc): Can we add a short checkpoint in three days to review initial canary metrics?
[12:33] Mark (Redwood): Yes, let's tentatively schedule Wed 2026-04-17 09:00 PT.
[12:40] Jason (BlueArc): Works for me.
[12:43] Tom (BlueArc): I'll need firewall info to start internal approvals.
[12:48] Luis (Redwood): Sending firewall/port list and a minimal network diagram after this call.
[12:55] [00:12:55] Priya (Redwood): Any other open questions?
[13:00] Jason (BlueArc): One final — do you log token-level timings in the hosted path? We might want token-level traces.
[13:10] Mark (Redwood): We have token timing traces for dedicated/private; hosted is sampled. We can enable more verbose sampling for the canary.
[13:22] Asha (BlueArc): Great, that helps.
[13:28] [00:13:28] Mark (Redwood): Ok team — we'll send the benchmark and docs; BlueArc will upload samples; schedule midweek rerun and checkpoint. Thanks everyone.
[13:40] (meeting ends)

Notes/Links referenced: trimmed-benchmark-runbook.md (link posted in chat), Private-deploy-network-checklist.pdf (will be shared), cost-model-hedge.xlsx (Luis to attach).
competitor_notes: Customer mentioned CloudEndpointX as a comparative vendor; they also discussed rolling their own on-prem stack as an alternate.
file_notes: Shared artifacts will be posted to the CRM record and Slack channel #bluearc-poc. No PII included in uploaded samples per customer.
